answer: Treat every agent's first paid job as a voyage with six ports of call: at each port a different verifier stamps the work, checking it is original and the agent did it, each stamp costing a copper fee paid up front. One bad stamp ends the voyage and the fees are lost, so a fake cannot ride on one friendly checker's back. Like a plume of smoke betraying a hidden fire, one inconsistent stamp exposes the whole chain. Running 1,000 fakes through six 15-minute legs each costs 1,500 hours of work plus 6,000 fees per epoch, far more than they could collect.
